critical_findings: 30-40 episodes of severe persistent vomiting over 20 hours with only mild epigastric burning before onset

acute coronary syndrome presenting without chest pain
acute hepatitis or pancreatitis as causes of the transaminitis/vomiting
wrong_dx_traps: gastritis (stated working differential)
hepatitis (stated working differential)

atrial fibrillation, irregularly irregular pulse 80-115

critical_findings: severe immobilizing thoracolumbar back pain after soccer, previously completely asymptomatic

no neurologic deficit, no skin inflammation/erythema over the region

critical_findings: one year of amnesia, personality changes, hostile attitudes, aggression, hallucinations, illusions

progression to urinary and fecal incontinence and speech difficulties; dysarthric, disoriented to place and time
necrotic, unhealed, deeply seated wounds on left knee and right big toe

sequelae of prior head trauma (MRI finding as red herring)
parkinsonian/bradykinetic neurodegenerative disease

critical_findings: one week of exertional dyspnea, orthopnea, productive cough; hypoxic with SpO2 71% on room air needing 6 L
proBNP 4056 pg/mL but echo shows diastolic dysfunction with preserved ejection fraction
diffuse bilateral infiltrates on CXR and diffuse ground-glass opacities with mediastinal lymphadenopathy on CT
no response to ceftriaxone/azithromycin, then piperacillin-tazobactam, vancomycin, levofloxacin; progressed to BiPAP-dependent hypoxemic respiratory failure and ICU transfer

vasculitis/pulmonary-renal syndrome (serologies sent, creatinine elevated)

diastolic congestive heart failure (diuretics given; proBNP as decoy)
pulmonary embolism (V/Q performed)

critical_findings: masseter pain for one year, occipital and left temporal scalp pain for three months, enlarged temporal artery for one month

bilateral enlarged temporal arteries with weak left-sided pulse

ESR markedly elevated at 113 mm/h
unknown etiology despite oral surgery and neurosurgery specialist consultations

giant cell arteritis as a systemic vasculitis with stroke risk
other causes of ischemic optic neuropathy and headache (must be excluded)
wrong_dx_traps: dental/oral surgical pathology (year of masseter pain, multiple specialist referrals)
neurosurgical cause for the occipital/headache complaints
isolated ophthalmologic disease followed without systemic workup

critical_findings: six months of progressive weakness beginning in the arms after gym exercise, worsening to neck muscles, improving on rest days
progression to inability to chew or close the jaw, nasal voice, difficulty swallowing with 5 kg weight loss
barium swallow: uncoordinated pharyngeal swallow with significant silent aspiration risk

bilateral facial weakness with forehead sparing, inability to close eyes, poor palatal movement; shoulder abduction fatiguing completely in under 20 repetitions; no ptosis or diplopia, full limb power
incidental anterior mediastinal soft tissue mass 4.5 x 2.5 cm on CT
normal mandibular X-ray/orthopantomogram and naso-endoscopy with normal vocal cord mobility; CT ruled out stroke and brainstem compression
dangerous_misses: myasthenic crisis with aspiration risk (barium swallow already shows silent aspiration)
mediastinal malignancy (lymphoma suspicion raised by the mass)
respiratory muscle involvement requiring monitoring

acetylcholine receptor antibody testing and repetitive nerve stimulation (mandated by fatigable bulbar weakness)
wrong_dx_traps: lymphoma as the initial suspicion from the mediastinal mass

stroke or brainstem compression (specifically ruled out on CT)

critical_findings: self-limiting watery diarrhea with fever, followed 10 days later by ascending weakness: proximal arms then legs, then distal arms
symmetric weakness graded MRC 3-4 in all four limbs; abolished triceps brachii reflexes with otherwise normal DTRs
no sensory dysfunction and no sphincter disturbance; cranial nerves unaffected
CSF protein 0.59 g/L (slightly elevated) with normal cell count 3 mononuclear cells/mm3
EMG at 3 weeks: polyphasic neuropathic muscle action potentials with reduced interference pattern; normal motor and sensory conduction velocities
normal muscle enzymes, glucose, electrolytes, serum protein
dangerous_misses: respiratory failure from ascending neuromuscular weakness (FVC monitoring mandated in Guillain-Barré syndrome)
autonomic instability during progression
cord compression or myelopathy as an alternative to peripheral weakness

Campylobacter jejuni stool/serologic testing (mandated by antecedent enteritis)
wrong_dx_traps: inflammatory myopathy/polymyositis (muscle pain in legs, back, shoulders; normal enzymes against it)
stroke or spinal cord lesion for the acute weakness
post-viral fatigue/deconditioning

critical_findings: ninth day postpartum with severe headache begun in the last trimester and worsened after delivery, then confusion and two generalized seizures
blood pressure 200/120
seizures continued despite magnesium sulfate bolus and hydralazine - refractory to presumed-eclampsia treatment
new left-sided weakness with declining level of consciousness

coagulation studies (PT 13.4 s/INR 1.1, PTT 45 s, D-dimer 550) within normal range; no intracerebral abnormality yet identified

intracranial hemorrhage in the setting of severe hypertension and refractory seizures
eclampsia itself (must be considered first, but refractoriness demands re-imaging)

wrong_dx_traps: postpartum eclampsia as the presumed diagnosis and treatment frame (magnesium and hydralazine given)
treatment-resistant eclampsia rather than a structural venous cause
hypertensive emergency alone explaining the focal deficit

critical_findings: acute-onset band-like headache with cervical spine radiation, beginning during the last minutes of vigorous exercise-bike workout, in a man with no prior headache history

subsequent normal MRI brain, cervical/thoracic/lumbar spine imaging, and MRA head and neck
no positional change, no meningeal signs, normal neurologic examination

cerebral venous sinus thrombosis

critical_findings: sudden left-sided visual loss lasting 5 minutes while stretching his neck, associated with headache
neck stretching/positioning immediately preceding the event

entirely normal neurologic and cranial nerve examination, GCS 15, normal confrontation visual fields

critical_findings: total parenteral nutrition for six and a half months with persistent nausea and vomiting preventing oral intake

critical_findings: stuporous at home with dyspnea and confusion; cold, painful, paresthetic right lower extremity with absent dorsalis pedis pulse

standard atherosclerotic multivessel disease (patient is a smoker)
anticoagulation failure alone rather than a provoking toxin

critical_findings: normochromic anemia Hb 78 g/L with elevated reticulocytes 5.7% and slight inconstant basophilic stippling of red cells
mildly elevated AST 44 and ALT 107

critical_findings: 15-year history of anxiety and depression on sertraline; blood pressures 146/103 and 140/80 attributed to anxiety

abdominal/adrenal imaging (mandated to localize any catecholamine source)

critical_findings: chronic primary hyperparathyroidism post-parathyroidectomy with calcium, phosphorus, and PTH stable for years off treatment

low anion gap 5 with albumin 2.7 and total protein 5.1
creatinine 1.97 above baseline 1.4-1.5; mild hypovolemia from vomiting and poor intake

SPEP and UPEP negative; symptoms persisted despite treatment

myeloma (SPEP/UPEP sent as decoy)

critical_findings: one year of rapidly increasing weight and appetite with headache, fatigue, proximal muscle weakness, easy bruising, purple abdominal striae

critical_findings: eight months of worsening bilateral hand tremors, falls, depressed mood with suicidal thoughts, altered mental status, dysphagia, double incontinence

wrong_dx_traps: lean NAFLD as the fixed liver diagnosis from six years earlier
alcohol dependence (question raised, adamantly denied)

critical_findings: 3 months of tender swollen hand, wrist, and ankle joints with fatigue; intermittent swelling since age 47 with morning stiffness up to an hour

critical_findings: six months of diffuse bone pain and proximal muscle weakness mainly in lower extremities and shoulders; unable to rise from a chair or climb stairs

calcium 7.6, phosphorus 1.9, alkaline phosphatase 866, 25-OH vitamin D 10 - low Ca, low phosphate, high ALP

celiac serology (anti-tissue transglutaminase) and duodenal biopsy (mandated by anemia + severe vitamin D deficiency without GI symptoms)
PTH (to complete the metabolic bone workup)

critical_findings: left upper extremity weakness on postoperative day 46 after subtotal esophagectomy for cT1b N0 M0 tumor; postoperative anastomotic leak managed with drainage

does not fulfill DIC diagnostic criteria
CA19-9 5594 and CA-125 277 markedly elevated

disseminated intravascular coagulation (criteria checked, not met)

abdominal imaging for occult pancreatic/hepatic malignancy (mandated by marker elevation)
wrong_dx_traps: cardioembolic stroke (fully worked up and excluded)

critical_findings: 20 days of generalized body swelling, headache, subconjunctival hemorrhage, treated for new-onset hypertension
five days of dyspnea at rest and hemoptysis with worsening hypoxia (SpO2 74% on room air) and acute kidney injury
serum creatinine 6.7, urea 210, with urinalysis showing many RBCs/HPF, 3+ proteinuria, and RBC casts
bibasilar end-inspiratory crepitations with bilateral middle and lower zone infiltrates on CXR; periorbital puffiness and pallor
